answer.rationale: Finance demands an 18% cut and the incumbent has refused to reopen price, so renewing at status quo fails the mandate. memory_c2 (low-cost vendor: sharp unit-cost cut, quick onboarding, accurate invoicing) is the directly applicable lever, but I am burning my single verification slot on memory_c6 instead because the multi-year volume-pricing pattern is the one that would most cleanly reconcile 'cost cut' with 'no delivery-risk increase' if I can frame the switch as a multi-year commitment to the new vendor. memory_c3 (second source removed single point of failure and held allocation through a shortage) supports the risk posture: even though I can only execute one decision this cycle, switching primary supply to a proven low-cost vendor is the highest-leverage single move for TCO. The 14-day expiry and 94% line utilisation with no buffer make deferral unacceptable; negotiate_terms is blocked by the incumbent's refusal; add_second_source alone does not deliver the 18% cut. Downstream risk flagged: the switch must include a validated transition window to protect the 94% assembly-line commitment, and uncertainty around the new vendor's performance at Halden's volumes is acknowledged and should be gated by the onboarding plan.
